issues.legal_issue: Atiyat courts have jurisdiction to investigate claims concerning the extent of an abolished grant when determining rights to commutation.
material_facts: The claimant sought commutation as a hissedar in a Paigah estate and argued that the Jagir Administrator’s role in calculating commutation left no room for a further inquiry into the extent of the grant.
The claimant relied on older reports, a royal order, and estate budgets as establishing the grant’s extent.
The government disputed whether all the lands claimed remained part of the grant, alleging that some had been submerged and compensated for and that other lands had been made into sub-grants.
An Atiyat court had investigated the claim and rejected part of it.
issues.conclusion: The Atiyat courts had jurisdiction to investigate the extent of the grant and the associated claims; the claimant’s evidence was for those courts to assess.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3A of the Hyderabad Atiyat Enquiries Act, 1952, as amended, assigns Atiyat courts inquiries into rights, title, or interest in the relevant grants and related succession claims. The Act’s definition of Atiyat grants includes commutation sums payable for abolished jagirs. The broad inquiry authority encompasses investigation of the grant’s extent where that extent must be ascertained to determine commutation; earlier reports and orders are evidence for the Atiyat court to weigh, not a substitute for its inquiry. The court relied on the stated purpose of the 1956 amendment that commutation payments depended on completing such inquiries. No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.claim_concerns_commutation_for_abolished: A claimant seeks commutation for an interest in a grant abolished by law.
predicates.grant_inquiry_authority_is_broad: The governing scheme assigns a specialized inquiry court authority to investigate rights, title, or interests in the grant and related matters.
predicates.extent_depends_on_evidentiary_inquiry: The extent of the grant relevant to commutation depends on evidence that may require assessment, including disputed changes to the lands or interests claimed.

issues.definition: When a commutation claim concerns an abolished grant, the governing scheme provides broad grant-inquiry authority, and the grant’s relevant extent depends on evidentiary assessment, the inquiry court may investigate that extent.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant challenging an Atiyat court’s decision must pursue the available appeal before the designated revenue appellate body, which may be directed to hear the appeal after allowing the claimant to submit material.
material_facts: After the Atiyat court rejected part of the claim, the claimant appealed to the Board of Revenue, then withdrew that appeal and filed writ petitions challenging the Atiyat court’s authority.
The High Court directed the Board of Revenue to re-entertain the appeal and decide it after giving the claimant an opportunity to submit material.
The Supreme Court considered the Board of Revenue the proper forum for adjudicating the dispute and upheld the High Court’s direction.
issues.conclusion: The High Court properly directed the Board of Revenue to re-entertain and decide the appeal after allowing the claimant to present material; that direction was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: The Commutation Regulation provides an appeal to the Board of Revenue from a determination of commutation, and the Atiyat Enquiries Act provides for appeals from decisions of Atiyat courts. The Board was the proper forum to adjudicate the challenge to the Atiyat court’s decision. No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.appeal_from_grant_inquiry_decision: A party seeks review of a specialized grant inquiry court’s decision.
predicates.specialized_revenue_body_has_appellate_a: The governing scheme gives a designated revenue body appellate authority over the challenged decision.
predicates.party_withdrew_appeal_to_pursue_writ_cha: The party withdrew an available appeal and instead challenged the inquiry court’s authority in writ proceedings.

issues.definition: When a party challenges a grant inquiry decision, an appellate revenue body has authority to review it, and the party withdrew that appeal to pursue a writ challenge, the revenue body must rehear the appeal while allowing material to be submitted.

issues.legal_issue: A court may decline to order interim allowance payments when the government offers payment subject to adequate security, the claimant declines to provide it, and the payments may exceed the final entitlement.
material_facts: The claimant sought an order for interim maintenance allowances.
The government stated that it was prepared to make the payments if the claimant furnished an adequate bank guarantee.
The interim allowances were adjustable against the final commutation sum, and the government asserted that the claimant had already received more than would ultimately be due.
The claimant was not prepared to furnish a bank guarantee.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to make any further order for interim payments.
issues.legal_principle: The Jagir Abolition Regulation provides for interim maintenance allowances pending determination of commutation, and the Commutation Regulation provides for adjustment of excess interim allowances against the final payment. In light of that adjustment and the government’s stated willingness to pay against adequate security, the Court found no basis to grant the requested order when the claimant declined to provide security. No earlier cases were cited.

rule.if: appeal_seeks_interim_allowance_order and interim_payments_are_adjustable_against_final_entitlement and government_conditions_payment_on_adequate_security and claimant_declines_security and government_asserts_prior_payments_exceed_final_entitlement

predicates.appeal_seeks_interim_allowance_order: A party asks the court in an appeal to order interim allowance payments.
predicates.interim_payments_are_adjustable_against_: The interim payments can be adjusted against the final amount due to the claimant.
predicates.government_conditions_payment_on_adequat: The government offers to make the interim payments if the claimant provides adequate security.
predicates.claimant_declines_security: The claimant is unwilling to provide the requested security.
predicates.government_asserts_prior_payments_exceed: The government asserts that payments already made exceed what will ultimately be due.

issues.definition: When an appeal seeks interim allowances that are adjustable against final entitlement, the government conditions payment on adequate security, the claimant declines that security, and the government asserts prior payments exceed final entitlement, the court may decline to order payment.
